pr_title: fix: panic when creating segment buffer reader
pr_body:
Calling `wal.NewSegmentBufReader()` without any segments would
cause panic resulting prometheus crashing. This patch fixes the panic by
returning an error if the no segments are passed.

Fixes: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/9605

Signed-off-by: Sunil Thaha <sthaha@redhat.com>
pr_comments: Is this a bug affecting Prometheus or just when tsdb is used as a library?
Is there a way to reproduce this that does not involve NFS?

> Is there a way to reproduce this that does not involve NFS?

No sorry, I haven't found a good way yet :( . I will look further.
Another thing to consider is what is the effect of this. Is prometheus able to start,is there data loss?

> Is there a way to reproduce this that does not involve NFS?

I can trigger the panic by removing manually all files from a checkpoint directory and starting Prometheus. When we discussed the original issue with @sthaha, our idea was that in such cases, Prometheus should exit with an error instead of panic'ing but maybe Prometheus could just handle this case and continue since there's no checkpoint to read anyway?

@simonpasquier thanks for chiming in 🙇
I was able to reproduce this by deleting the files from `data/wal/checkpoint.*` but noticed an interesting behaviour when testing using the latest `main` (be2599c85384). Prometheus would crash every other time and  it correlated with  the presence/absence of `data/lock` file.

Edit: Please Ignore the above. It seems to like another bug related to how `cfg.localStoragePath` gets initialised to either `data-agent` or `data` randomly due to `cfg.localStoragePath` begin used for both `storage.tsdb.path` and `storage.agent.path` 

```go
	a.Flag("storage.tsdb.path", "Base path for metrics storage.").
		PreAction(serverOnlySetting()).
		Default("data/").StringVar(&cfg.localStoragePath)
	a.Flag("storage.agent.path", "Base path for metrics storage.").
		PreAction(agentOnlySetting()).
		Default("data-agent/").StringVar(&cfg.localStoragePath)
```

<details> 
<summary> This reproduces the issue seen </summary>

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"

	kingpin "gopkg.in/alecthomas/kingpin.v2"
)

func main() {

	var dataPath string
	var gotAgent, gotData bool

	for !(gotData && gotAgent) {

		a := kingpin.New("foobar", "test parsing").UsageWriter(os.Stderr)

		a.Flag("storage.tsdb.path", "Base path for metrics storage.").
			Default("data/").StringVar(&dataPath)

		a.Flag("storage.agent.path", "Base path for metrics storage.").
			Default("data-agent/").StringVar(&dataPath)

		if _, err := a.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("parse error")
		}

		if !gotData && dataPath == "data/" {
			fmt.Println("got data")
			gotData = true
		}
		if !gotAgent && dataPath == "data-agent/" {
			fmt.Println("got data-agent")
			gotAgent = true
		}

	}
}
```
</details>
@roidelapluie  is this expected?

That last point about `cfg.localStoragePath` will be fixed in main soon #9676.

In the past, we have generally not handled gracefully the cases that should not be possible e.g. empty checkpoint dir. It should not happen because we create temporary directoires and use the atomic RENAME syscall once they are populated correctly.
@roidelapluie Thanks for explanation. I will close this PR.

> **What did you do?** Run prometheus (deployed using Prometheus Operator in Kubernetes) using NFS for persistent storage. Although NFS is unsupported, it shouldn't result in prometheus crashing.

I am sorry but this is exactly what it means: NFS can cause Prometheus to crash, which is why it is not supported.
ping @codesome what should we do about this issue? thanks

If avoiding the crash would (1) require a ~small update in code (2) and _not_ assume a non-POSIX storage, then happy to accept contributions for that. Otherwise, I don't think it is worth updating the error handling for non-POSIX storage since that would fill the codebase with lots of code that assumes that storage can be non-POSIX (like every interaction with the storage?).

If #9606 fixes it, that looks like an acceptable patch (but needs some changes, like `NewSegmentBufReader` should not return an error for 0 segments, but rather the reader should return `io.EOF` error when tried to read)
